skill.description: Designs paid advertising account structures, including campaign type selection, ad groups, targeting, match types, exclusions, and paid versus organic overlap checks.

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives from Markdown fences, inline code formatting, repository-relative links, and public documentation URLs. No evidence found of executable commands, hidden network calls, path traversal, prompt injection, or malicious intent in SKILL.md. The skill does handle user ad exports and writes confirmed summaries, so filename sanitization and user authorization should remain explicit.

remediation.suggestion: State that account or goal values must be slugified before saving under memory/ad/campaign-architect/.

remediation.issue: Optional external ad platform connectors are mentioned in the instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Keep connector use read-only and require explicit user authorization before accessing any ad account data.

content.value_statement: Paid advertising accounts waste budget when campaign types, ad groups, and keywords overlap. This skill creates a structured launch or audit plan with targeting, exclusions, and ROAS audience scoring.
actual_capabilities: Chooses campaign types such as Search, PMax, or broad match based on goals.
Maps ad groups and asset groups around single intent themes.
Plans targeting, audience signals, and match types for each campaign area.
Builds negative keyword, placement exclusion, and audience exclusion recommendations.
Compares paid query themes with organic traffic data to flag overlap.
Scores the ROAS audience dimension and prepares a handoff summary.
limitations: Does not calculate the final RQS or enforce full account veto rules.
Does not create budget allocation or spend split recommendations.
Needs user-provided exports, goals, or pasted campaign details for accurate work.
External ad platform APIs are optional and must be authorized by the user.

use_cases.title: Launch a paid search account
use_cases.description: Create a first campaign structure with campaign types, ad groups, match types, and negatives.

use_cases.title: Audit paid and organic overlap
use_cases.description: Compare paid query themes with organic landing page data to find waste and cannibalization.

use_cases.title: Rebuild messy ad groups
use_cases.description: Separate overlapping themes, define asset groups, and create cleaner exclusion rules.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new account.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a paid account structure for my goal: [goal]. Platform: [platform]. Product or service themes: [themes].

prompt_templates.title: Choose Campaign Type
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate choice between Search, PMax, and broad match.
prompt_templates.prompt: Should this goal use Search, PMax, broad match, or a mix? Explain the tradeoffs and propose campaign groups.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Overlap and Negatives
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review using campaign and analytics exports.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit paid and organic overlap using my campaign export, search terms, and GA4 traffic data. Recommend negatives and exclusions.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Full Handoff Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced structure plan ready for account audit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the full campaign structure, targeting plan, negative list, ROAS audience score, and handoff summary for this account.

output_examples.input: Plan a Google Ads launch for a B2B demo request goal.
output: Recommended Search campaigns for high-intent demo terms and competitor terms.
Separate ad groups by problem, product category, and brand intent.
Negative keywords for jobs, free tools, education, and unsupported regions.

output_examples.input: Audit paid and organic overlap from campaign and GA4 exports.
output: Flags paid themes where organic landing pages already capture demand.
Separates incremental paid coverage from likely cannibalized brand traffic.
Lists exclusions and follow-up data needed for uncertain themes.

output_examples.input: Choose Search, PMax, or broad match for ecommerce product groups.
output: Recommends PMax where feed quality and creative coverage are strong.
Keeps Search for high-control product and brand intent groups.
Explains where broad match needs stronger conversion history first.

best_practices: Provide campaign goals, platform, conversion type, and current structure before asking for a plan.
Share search-term and GA4 exports when auditing overlap or negative keywords.
Review recommended negatives and exclusions before applying them in an ad platform.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to calculate a full RQS score or account-level veto result.
Do not use it as the sole source for budget allocation.
Do not paste sensitive exports without removing unrelated customer or employee data.

faq.question: Can it choose between Search and PMax?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares the goal, intent maturity, feed readiness, and control needs before recommending a campaign type.

faq.question: Does it connect directly to Google Ads?
faq.answer: It can work from manual exports. Optional read-only connectors should be used only with user authorization.

faq.question: Does it calculate campaign budgets?
faq.answer: No. It delegates budget allocation to a separate budget optimizer and focuses on account structure.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the business goal, platform, product themes, current campaigns, search terms, and GA4 traffic data when available.

faq.question: Can it audit paid and organic cannibalization?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares paid query themes against organic landing page traffic and flags likely overlap.

faq.question: Does it replace the ad account auditor?
faq.answer: No. It produces the structure and ROAS audience score for the auditor to roll into the full review.
